# Idempotent creation of the payment row

> A single SQL insert at the start of `executePayment` that creates the `Payment` row with `ON CONFLICT ("idempotencyKey") DO NOTHING`, then reads the row back, so retried or duplicate messages share one payment.

_Part of [Charging a card through Stripe](charging-a-payment.md)_

The first thing `executePayment` (in [`PaymentService`](charging-a-payment.md)) does is open a short database transaction and try to insert a new `Payment` row. The row starts in `PENDING` status and carries the idempotency key, the amount, the order id and the user id. The idempotency key is the request ID that identifies this one purchase attempt. If a row with that key already exists, the insert does nothing and raises no error. This happens when the user spams the API or when Kafka redelivers the message. Right after the insert, in the same transaction, the code reads the payment back by idempotency key through `PaymentDtoService.requestPayment`. The first message and any duplicate both get the same row. If the server dies before the transaction commits, it rolls back. The Kafka offset does not move, so the message is retried and the row is created again. If the server dies just after the commit, the row stays `PENDING` and the next attempt picks it up. If the row is already `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`, `executePayment` returns it right away. `PENDING` and `UNKNOWN` rows carry on to the Stripe charge.

**Look at:** [`PaymentService.executePayment` in payment.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/application/payment.service.ts#L65)

## Pieces

- [Insert that silently skips when the idempotency key already exists](insert-on-conflict-do-nothing.md): A raw SQL `INSERT INTO "Payment"` with a generated id and `PENDING` status, ending in `ON CONFLICT ("idempotencyKey") DO NOTHING`.
- [Read-back of the payment row in the same transaction](payment-dto-service.md): After the insert, `requestPayment` loads the row by idempotency key together with its order, so new and duplicate messages get the same payment.
- [Early return for payments already finished](payment-status.md): If the loaded payment is neither `PENDING` nor `UNKNOWN`, `executePayment` returns it without charging again.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | `"Payment" table` | Receives the insert with `ON CONFLICT ("idempotencyKey") DO NOTHING`, then is read back by idempotency key. This relies on a unique constraint on `idempotencyKey`. |
| queue | `Kafka (via `[`KafkaTopicGroup`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/infrastructure/outbox/outbox.model.ts#L14)` topic passed in)` | The consumer's retry behaviour is what makes the dedup matter: if the transaction rolls back, the offset does not move and the message is redelivered. |

## Also relies on

- [Payment records and DTO service](payment-records.md): Relies on the `Payment` model, its `PENDING` status and `PaymentDtoService.requestPayment` to read the row back.
- [Charging a card through Stripe](charging-a-payment.md): This is the first step of the charging flow, which continues to stock checks and Stripe after the row exists.

## Watch out

- The insert and the read-back run in one transaction. Without the read-back you would not get the existing row when the insert is skipped.
- `DO NOTHING` returns no row and no error, so the code cannot tell from the insert whether it created the row. It reads the row back and checks its status.
- An `UNKNOWN` payment is not returned early. It continues and resends to Stripe with the same idempotency key, which returns the original outcome instead of charging twice.
- The insert uses raw SQL through `sequelizeInstance.query`, not the model, so the columns (`id` from `gen_random_uuid()`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`) are set by hand.
